finding.claim: /fetch2 performs a full-read SSRF: the URL is checked only for an http/https scheme, so internal hosts, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints are reachable, and the first 200 characters of the response are returned to the caller.
finding.source: views.py:19 request.args.get("url") — unauthenticated HTTP query parameter
finding.sink: views.py:22 requests.get(url, timeout=5) with default allow_redirects=True

trace.note: scheme-only check; no hostname or IP validation
is_http_url gate passes for http://127.0.0.1, RFC1918, 169.254.169.254
requests.get follows redirects, so a public URL redirecting to an internal address also bypasses any check
response .text[:200] returned in JSON body; readable, not blind

finding.guards_checked: Only is_http_url (scheme check). No hostname, IP, port, or redirect restriction. allow_redirects not disabled. No auth on the route.

verdict.guard_found: None on the /fetch2 path. views.py:20 applies only is_http_url, and validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check (urlparse(url).scheme in ("http", "https")). The hostname/IP check is is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18), but /fetch2 does not call it. The /fetch route at views.py:12 does call it, which is the contrast that shows /fetch2 is missing the guard. views.py:22 uses requests.get with default allow_redirects, so redirects are followed without re-checking.
verdict.reason: The url comes from an unauthenticated query parameter (views.py:19), is gated only by the scheme-only is_http_url check (views.py:20, validators.py:7), and is fetched with redirects enabled at views.py:22 with the first 200 characters returned in the response (views.py:22), so the finding holds.

finding.claim: /fetch is vulnerable to DNS rebinding (TOCTOU): the hostname is resolved and checked by is_safe_url, but requests.get resolves it again without pinning the checked address, so a short-TTL attacker-controlled DNS record can return a public IP for the check and an internal IP for the fetch.
finding.source: views.py:11 request.args.get("url") — unauthenticated HTTP query parameter; DNS answers controlled by attacker-owned nameserver

trace.note: requests.get performs DNS lookup #2 on the same hostname, not pinned to the validated IP; rebinding returns 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254

finding.guards_checked: is_safe_url: scheme, hostname presence, getaddrinfo IP check for private/loopback/link-local/reserved. allow_redirects=False closes the redirect path. No IP pinning, no Host-header-preserving connect to validated address.

verdict.guard_found: none. validators.py:12-18 checks scheme and resolved IPs only, with no IP pinning; views.py:14 calls requests.get(url) with the hostname, so it resolves DNS again. allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) only closes the redirect path. Nothing in views.py:11-14 pins the validated address.
verdict.reason: The url comes unauthenticated from request.args at views.py:11, is_safe_url at validators.py:14-16 resolves and checks the hostname, and requests.get at views.py:14 resolves it a second time with no pinned IP, so a short-TTL rebinding record can pass the check and then fetch an internal address. Every trace line matches the code. The finding is a real TOCTOU, and no closing guard exists.
